# Schema Infrastructure v2.0: The Complete Guide

The schema system is the nervous system of the OpenCode ecosystem. Every factory, every skill, every signal, every deferred option -- all described by schemas that describe themselves. This is a tour of the architecture, the hierarchies, and the unification pipeline.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Diagram" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:900px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;">

## The Core Insight

The schema system emerged from one problem: **7 schema files across 4 separate locations with massive field duplication**. The `signal_tracking` block was identically duplicated in 4 places. Every schema had its own copy of `id`, `title`, `status`, `priority`, `created`, `updated`, `description`. When you update one, you must remember to update three others. This is drift risk.

The solution: a **7-layer architecture** with recursive self-description. The schemas describe themselves using a meta-schema.

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Diagram" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:900px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;">

## The Inheritance Hierarchy

The tree flows from:

### base-entity (8 fields)

Root of the entire hierarchy -- every entity schema inherits:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | string (kebab-case) | Unique identifier |
| `title` | string (max 200) | Human-readable name |
| `status` | enum | Lifecycle status |
| `priority` | enum | high / medium / low |
| `created` | datetime (ISO8601) | Creation timestamp |
| `updated` | datetime (ISO8601) | Last modification |
| `description` | object | intent, scope, success_criteria |
| `tags` | array of strings | Categorization |

### The 4 Mixins

| Mixin | Adds | Used By |
|-------|------|---------|
| **mixin-schedulable** | schedule, deadlines, recurrence, reminders | project, research, goal |
| **mixin-trackable** | roadmap + dashboard + signal_tracking | project, research, agent |
| **mixin-traceable** | change_history (every mutation recorded) | project, research, agent, goal, deferred, task |
| **mixin-relatable** | parent/child relationships, cross-refs | project, research, agent |

### The Resulting Field Composition

| Schema | Base | Mixins | Own Fields | Total |
|--------|------|--------|------------|-------|
| project-schema | 8 | 4 | phases, context, menu | 42 |
| research-schema | 8 | 4 | adapters, sources, findings, history | 47 |
| agent-schema | 8 | 3 | identity, tools, parameters, harness | 31 |
| goal-schema | 8 | 2 | subtasks, category, reminder_sent | 17 |
| deferred-schema | 8 | 1 | source, trigger, dates | 15 |
| task-schema | 8 | 1 | action, params, result, error | 16 |

## Field Overlap Analysis

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Diagram" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:900px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;">

Before composition, high overlap without shared structure meant drift risk. After composition, overlaps are explicit via shared base/mixin references. The heatmap shows which schema pairs share the most fields and how composition eliminated hidden duplication.

## Signal Unification Pipeline

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Diagram" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:900px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;">

**10 distinct signal types** flowing from **7 ad-hoc formats** into a single Pydantic-validated pipeline:

| Signal Type | Old Storage | New Location |
|-------------|------------|--------------|
| menu-present/select | signals.json | PG + Directus |
| trigger-usage | trigger_usage.json | PG + Directus |
| co-selection | co_selections.json | PG + Directus |
| menu-violation | menu_violations.jsonl | PG + Directus |
| deferred-option | deferred_options.json | PG + Directus |
| flow-event | hybrid_tracker.py to PG | Unified PG table |
| memory-op | pghmem to PG | Unified PG table |
| schema-change | controlplane | Unified PG table |
| resource-mutation | controlplane | Unified PG table |

The PostgreSQL schema uses a single table with JSONB payload for type-specific fields. This enables portability to pi mono (ARM, limited disk), schema evolution without ALTER TABLE, and natural Directus compatibility.

## Pydantic Model Hierarchy

<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," alt="Diagram" style="display:block;width:100%;max-width:900px;height:auto;margin:1.5rem auto;">

Every signal type gets its own Pydantic class extending `BaseSignal`. The `SIGNAL_MODELS` dict maps `SignalType` enum values to their models. This gives us:

1. **Type validation** at creation time
2. **Serialization** for PG and JSON writes
3. **Portability** across server and pi mono
4. **Directus compatibility** via JSON mapping

## Meta-Schema

The meta-schema is the constitution. It defines what valid schemas look like. Every schema in the ecosystem must validate against it. The structure has 5 sections:

| Section | Fields | Purpose |
|---------|--------|---------|
| **Identity** | id, version, type, description | kebab-case IDs, semver, schema type |
| **Composition** | extends, mixins, imports | Inheritance and composition rules |
| **Ecosystem** | consumers, lifecycle | Which skills use it, how mature |
| **Evolution** | changelog array | Every change with action, field, date |
| **Validation** | field types, patterns, required | Schema-level validation rules |

### How a Schema Declares Itself

Every schema file starts with a metadata header:

```yaml
$id: project-schema
$version: 2.0.0
$type: entity
$extends: base-entity
$mixins: [schedulable, trackable, traceable, relatable]
$imports: [roadmap-schema, dashboard-schema]
$consumers: [project-factory, orchestrator]
$lifecycle: stable
```

Then it only defines the fields THIS schema adds beyond base and mixins. No more duplication.

## Health Scoring

The schema system scores health across 5 dimensions:

| Dimension | Weight | What It Measures |
|-----------|--------|-----------------|
| Composition | 30% | Are schemas using base-entity plus mixins? |
| Dedup | 25% | How much field duplication remains? |
| Coverage | 20% | Are all schemas registered and self-describing? |
| Freshness | 15% | Are schemas recently validated/updated? |
| Integration | 10% | Do schemas declare consumers correctly? |

**Target: greater than 90 within one month.**

## Why This Matters

This is not just about organizing YAML files. It is about **making the system self-aware**. When every schema declares what it extends, what it mixes, who consumes it, and how it changes -- the system can:

- Detect drift automatically
- Suggest composition improvements before they become problems
- Generate health reports without human intervention
- Ensure every 7B model reading a schema instantly understands its position
- Port to pi mono with zero field-level changes

```
schemas/

├── base-entity.yaml             # root entity (8 fields)
├── mixin-schedulable.yaml       # scheduling
├── mixin-trackable.yaml         # progress tracking
├── mixin-traceable.yaml         # change history
├── mixin-relatable.yaml         # relationships
├── signal-tracking-schema.yaml  # extracted sub-schema
├── schema-registry.yaml         # auto-generated
├── schema-history.yaml          # ecosystem changelog
└── pydantic_models.py           # unified Pydantic
```

</details>
